one_liner: Sherlock (sherlock-project) is a local open-source Python CLI for username enumeration across sites; it has no hosted HTTP API or credentials, so it can't become a standard hosted-API toolkit.
auth_notes: The local tool needs no API keys or login. Other products named Sherlock (Sherlock Interview API, CloudFerro, Aleph Alpha) are unrelated and use bearer tokens.
access_notes: The open-source CLI is free to install and run locally, with no account. There is no vendor-hosted service to get credentials for.
blocker_notes: It is a local CLI that sends requests directly to each target site. There is no hosted API, so a toolkit would need to run the CLI itself, for example through a community MCP wrapper. Its traffic may also be seen as scraping.

evidence.quote: Sherlock is designed to be straightforward for open source investigations: it does not require API keys or login credentials for the sites it checks
No account/API keys needed** – Sherlock uses direct web requests and does not require creating any account or API key to use.
it simply constructs the expected profile URL for each site and observes the response to determine whether the username exists on a given platform.
